dedupe_keys.name: cepri guide le secteur de la sante face au risque d inondation health sector and flood risk with french hospital flood experience

description: This French guide from CEPRI, the European centre for flood risk prevention, sets out why hospitals and other health establishments are vulnerable to floods and how they can prepare. It notes that France's 2011 preliminary flood risk assessment counted about 2,500 health establishments in flood zones, and that many more are exposed indirectly through their supplies of electricity, water and district heating and through road access. Chapters cover the health effects of floods, the legal context, the vulnerability of health buildings, flood plans and exercises, and the return to normal. It includes testimonies and experience from flooded French hospitals, such as recovery times after flooding: at Draguignan it took seven months to rehabilitate three floors. The 56-page guide is free to download as a PDF, in French. Coverage is France, with events cited up to 2018. Caveats: an awareness guide, not a dataset, no licence is stated, and the recovery figures are single accounts, not a systematic survey. Simulation uses: functional loss and recovery-time parameters for flooded hospitals, and checklists of dependencies for health facility flood models. Related records: the Førde hospital flood protection case (case_study-forde-hospital-flood-protection) shows a physical adaptation response to the same hazard.
